scope: One parameter-dependent anisotropic norm coefficient for all actual fixed-M j=1 candidate primes
proved: For the complete candidate set S_M of primes in [(4M+3)/3,(3M-1)/2], one can choose local least nonsquares and CRT-interpolate a single integer d_M with 1<=d_M<B_M that is a nonsquare modulo every candidate prime.
The CRT construction uses every candidate prime and no information about the unknown collision subset.

For the raw norm Rcal_M=C0(M)^2-d_M C1(M)^2, every noncollision candidate prime has exact valuation two and every collision prime has valuation at least four; p^4 divides Rcal_M iff the full gate collides.
For the normalized norm Ncal_M=Cbar0(M)^2-d_M Cbar1(M)^2, p divides Ncal_M iff the full gate collides, and a collision gives p^2 divisibility.
The collision radical is gcd(rad(abs(Ncal_M)),B_M) whenever the specialized pair is nonzero.
The norm is nonzero for a nonzero coefficient pair because a simultaneous nonsquare d_M cannot be a perfect square integer.
The direct CRT coefficient has log height at most M/6+o(M).
If log height(d_M)=delta M+o(M), the raw norm estimated componentwise gives collision-radical ratio at best H/2+delta/4.
The direct CRT value delta<=1/6 gives ratio H/2+1/24=3.20548043938709..., and a subexponential coefficient only recovers H/2=3.16381377272042....
The normalized norm ratio is H-kappa+delta/2 and is worse than the raw norm ratio.
All inherited norm ratios are much larger than the raw j=1 log mass 1/6 per M.

A row-dependent rational norm rule must prove denominator units and nonsquare symbols on every row; separate local norms do not form one exact scalar, while CRT aggregation returns to the same coefficient-height ledger.
The simple rules h, s, h+s, 2h+3s, M, M-1, and M+1 each have an exact actual arithmetic false-positive norm zero.
No general no-go is claimed for every bounded-complexity rational function of h,s,M.
Item149 de-overlap leaves the fixed-j=1 ceiling unchanged at 1/36 per 6M.
